newsitem.title: USA: Blast near Washington Planned Parenthood clinic.
newsitem.headline: Blast near Washington Planned Parenthood clinic.

text.p: An explosion occurred outside a Planned Parenthood clinic in downtown Washington on Wednesday on the anniversary of the Roe vs. Wade decision legalising abortion, a police spokesman said.
The blast went off at about 7:45 a.m. EST (1245 GMT) near the clinic at 16th and M Sts NW, about five blocks from the White House.
Witnesses told police they saw a short, Hispanic man run away after something exploded in his hand. There was no immediate report of any injuries.
Police, FBI and other federal agents closed off the street near the clinic as bomb-sniffing dogs searched the area.

The police spokesman said that some sort of suspicious "devices" were also found in back of the nearby Mayflower Hotel where Vice President Al Gore is scheduled to speak to a National Abortion Rights Action League lunch on Wednesday.
Police and fire officials said there was a lot of debris on the street outside the building that houses the clinic and they were checking to see if there were any injuries.

Anti-abortion groups are marking the 24th anniversary of the Supreme Court decision, which made abortion through all nine months of pregnancy legal, with meetings and statements calling for its repeal.
A spokesman for Planned Parenthood said that no one in their building has been injured by the explosion, which occured before its regular office hours.
Local television reported from the scene that police said they had found no injured people at the scene but they were checking with area hospitals to find out if anyone came in for treatment.
